div.head: Excom I 6.4
div.ab: Quodsi has tres ammonitiones et pias correptiones contempnit et satisfacere despicit, post hæc sit tibi, inquit, sicut ethnicus et publicanus, id est gentilis atque paganus, ut non iam pro Christiano, sed pro pagano habeatur’.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 432 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann prints in larger type (the readings of MS Ti, his note b on p. 432): et | publicanus

note.seg: et p. fehlt Reg Mart; steht in Burchardi Decr. XI 2, das Reg folgt
et p. missing in Reg Mart; present in Burchardi Decr. XI 2, which follows Reg

div.ab: But if he despises these three admonitions and loving rebukes and disdains to make satisfaction, after this let him be to you, he says, as the heathen and the publican, that is a gentile and pagan, so that he is held no longer as a Christian but as a pagan'.
